title: Introduce invocation entropy prioritizer and prefetch warmup metering
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds entropy-prioritized trace sampling and a Prefetch Warmup Metering dashboard; tunes token-decay alerts to reduce noise and improve SLO signal quality.

Expose invocation_ratio metric and hook into runtime emission path
Add Prefetch Warmup Metering dashboard and example panels
Tune token-decay SLO alert thresholds and add suppression window

description:
Context and motivation:
This change introduces an entropy-driven prioritizer for trace sampling to bias collection toward invocations with high output entropy (a proxy for higher information content and failure likelihood). The goal is to improve signal-to-noise in long-tail SLO investigations without increasing overall ingestion costs. In parallel, we add a Prefetch Warmup Metering dashboard that helps SREs and runtime engineers understand effectiveness of prefetch/warmup heuristics and their impact on token-level cost and tail latency. Finally, we tune token-decay alert thresholds to reduce false positives caused by short-lived traffic spikes.

What this PR does (single continuous description):
- Adds an entropy sampler (observability/tracing/entropy_sampler.go) that computes per-invocation entropy from token logits or token probability distributions, normalizes the score per model family, and produces a priority weight used by the adaptive trace sampling queue. Implementation uses a rolling median absolute deviation (MAD) per model family to keep normalization robust to outliers.
- Introduces invocation_context_ratio (server/invocation_metrics.go) — a compact metric that captures the fraction of prefetched tokens versus total invocation tokens; emitted at the end of invocation. This helps correlate prefetch effectiveness with downstream tail latency and cost.
- Provides a Prefetch Warmup Metering dashboard (dashboards/prefetch-warmup-dashboard.json) with panels for invocation_context_ratio distribution, warmup success rate (measured by early token cache hits), prefetch-induced latency delta, and correlated entropy percentiles.
- Tunes token-decay SLO alert rules (alerts/token-decay-slo.yml): increases aggregation window for low-traffic tenants, adds a 3-minute quiet window to suppress transients from deployment bursts, and lowers alert sensitivity for invocations under a token threshold.
- Adds docs explaining entropy sampling design and migration notes (docs/observability/entropy-sampling.md).
- Updates CI to validate telemetry schema and dashboard JSON against the new metric name.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Implementation of entropy prioritizer and runtime hook
- [x] Unit tests for sampler normalization and edge cases
- [x] Emission of invocation_context_ratio and dashboard wiring
- [x] Alert tuning and runbook suggestions
- [x] Documentation and migration notes
- [x] CI updates and green pipeline

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests included (tests/telemetry/entropy_sampler_test.go) cover normalization across synthetic logits and minimum invocation lengths.
- Local e2e against small dev cluster: verified that high-entropy invocations are sampled more often (sample rate for top 5% entropy increased from 1.2x to ~6x under adaptive budget) and overall trace ingestion stayed within configured budget.
- Dashboard panels validated with synthetic metrics exported from a replay harness; sample screenshots attached in the internal Linear ticket.

Rollout plan and risk mitigation:
- Feature is behind a feature flag (telemetry.entropy_prioritizer.enabled) defaulting to off for existing tenants. We will enable for internal tenancy first, then a small canary, and finally global rollout.
- Metrics migration: invocation_context_ratio replaces the older invocation_prefetch_ratio metric; dashboards include a compatibility layer and a migration note.
- Alert tuning will be enabled as a separate flag; rollout includes a 24-hour shadow period before firing page rules to avoid on-call churn.

Operational notes and runbook updates:
- Added a short runbook section in docs/observability/entropy-sampling.md describing how to interpret entropy percentiles and how to temporarily disable prioritizer for a tenant if it causes unexpected sampling concentration.
- Prefetch Warmup dashboard includes export links to CSV for quick offline analysis.

CI summary:
- ci/telemetry-checks.yml updated to assert presence and schema of invocation_context_ratio and entropy sample tag.
- Full telemetry test suite (unit + small e2e replay) passed on linux/amd and linux/arm after reruns.

Review conversation (high level):
- Addressed reviewer questions about normalization and metric naming.
- Resolved CI flakes by widening test timeouts in the replay harness.

Merge outcome:
- Merged to main with squash on 2026-03-04 after approvals and green CI.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-2118: schedule a week-long canary and capture pre/post token-cost and tail-latency deltas for the canary tenants.
- Instrument telemetry to emit sampler budget utilization metric (future PR).
- Add an alert that monitors sampler concentration imbalance (to detect if a small subset of calls consumes disproportionate sampling budget).
notes: This PR prioritizes observability signal quality while keeping ingestion budgets fixed.
Metric rename handled with a compatibility shim to avoid breaking dashboards immediately.
Feature flagged for controlled rollout; see ENG-2118 for canary plan.
